articles.title: Pressure mounts on struggling Marnus Labuschagne after Australia ODI axe falls
articles.summary: Batter dropped from white-ball tour to Zimbabwe and South Africa. Chief selector George Bailey insists his Test chances still alive. The once-glittering international cricket career of Marnus Labuschagne is on the ropes after he was dropped from the ODI side, even if chair of selectors George…
body: Labuschagne was dropped from Australia’s white-ball touring party to Zimbabwe and South Africa, a squad named with next year’s ODI World Cup in mind.

Australia play six ODIs in Zimbabwe and South Africa later this month before the highly-anticipated three-Test series against the Proteas in October. Selectors on Tuesday named a group of 17 for the ODI series, noting a squad for the Test will be announced in coming weeks.
Labuschagne was one of five players dropped from the team who played Bangladesh in Australia’s most recent ODI in June.
The 32-year-old was ranked by the ICC as the best batter in the world in 2023, but since then has averaged under 30 in Tests. In the latest rankings he came in at equal 38th.

articles.title: Australian tennis battlers savour ‘crazy’ pay days at US Open
articles.summary: Kim Birrell, Maya Joint and James Duckworth advance on day two. Birrell plans to spend $265,000 pay day on upcoming wedding. An elated Kim Birrell plans on paying down her mortgage after surviving a match point and a restless night’s sleep to chalk up a life-changing US Open win in New York.
body: The gritty Gold Coaster wore down Croatian Petra Marcinko 3-6, 7-6 (7-4), 6-3 to finally reach the second round after losing all three of her previous Flushing Meadows openers in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
Young gun Maya Joint and veteran James Duckworth also advanced on a banner day two for the Australian contingent.

Joint rallied to take out higher-ranked Russian Liudmila Samsonova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 to continue her revival after a horror start to 2026, while Duckworth notched a mighty 5-7, 6-3, 6-2, 7-6 (10-8) comeback victory over 2026 French Open semi-finalist Matteo Arnaldi, the men’s 30th seed.
But a beaming Birrell stole the day in burying her first-round hoodoo after being forced to return to Court 7 following a nervy 14-hour rain delay.

articles.title: Wu to face Wilson in British Open second round
articles.summary: World champion Wu Yize sets up a tie against Kyren Wilson at the British Open, with many big names progressing through round one in Cheltenham.
body: World champion Wu Yize set up an intriguing second-round tie against former Crucible winner Kyren Wilson at the British Open after both won their opening matches.
China's Wu beat compatriot Liu Hongyu 4-3 in Cheltenham, while 2024 world champion Wilson was a 4-1 winner against Austria's Florian Nuessle.
Last year's British Open champion Shaun Murphy was joined by Ding Junhui, Barry Hawkins, Judd Trump and John Higgins in progressing to the second round.
However, three-time world champion Mark Williams lost 4-0 to David Gilbert, world number two Neil Robertson fell 4-1 to Pang Junxu, and 2023 world champion Luca Brecel fell 4-3 to Chris Wakelin.

articles.title: Harry Edward, Britain’s first black Olympic medallist, inducted into England Athletics hall of fame
articles.summary: Edward and Mo Farah among those to be inducted. Sonia Lannaman and Shirley Strong also honoured. Britain’s first black Olympic medal winner Harry Edward is to be inducted into the England Athletics Hall of Fame.
body: Edward was until recent years a forgotten hero of the 1920s, a decade that saw him win two bronze edals, in the 100m and 200m, at the 1920 Antwerp Olympics. He was also three times the AAA 100yd and 220yd champion and won the 100, 220 and 440-yard AAA championships in 1922, inside a single hour. King George V came down from the stands to personally congratulate him.
Soon afterwards he emigrated to the US and disappeared from view. When he died in 1973 not a single British newspaper published a line to mark his passing.

Born and raised in Berlin, he was forging a promising career as a teenage sprinter when the first world war began. His father came from the British colony of Dominica, so Edward was arrested and interned. After the war he went to London, joined the Polytechnic Harriers and ran for Britain in the Olympics. Harold Abrahams, the British sprinter immortalised in Chariots of Fire, regarded him as one of the greatest sprinters he ever saw. He never beat him.

Any switch for the 24-year-old appears contingent on Matias Fernandez-Pardo completing a £51m move from Lille. The 21-year-old Belgium international was top of Jaissle’s wish list and is due in Newcastle for a medical. He can play across the front line, including as a No 10.

Woltemade is unlikely to be the only player leaving before the deadline on Tuesday night. The winger Jacob Murphy is wanted by Nottingham Forest, Nick Pope – Jaissle’s third-choice goalkeeper – is looking for a new club and Besiktas retain an interest in Joe Willock.

Pope, who started last season as Howe’s first choice and harboured then-realistic ambitions to be part of England’s World Cup squad, wants first-team football after falling behind the new signings Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen.Willock has impressed Jaissle and, despite offers from Istanbul, an exit that looked inevitable under Howe may be postponed.

articles.title: Arteta joins elite 250 club - but where does he rank?
articles.summary: At full-time in Arsenal's 1-0 win at Aston Villa, the travelling supporters sang about how their team will win the league again with Mikel Arteta in charge.
body: When thinking of the greatest managers of the Premier League era, Arsene Wenger, Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola are names that belong high on the list.
They are three of the rare breed to have managed 250 games with a single Premier League club, and Mikel Arteta is now the 10th member of that elite group.
Monday's 1-0 win over Aston Villa was the 250th top-flight game in charge for Arteta with the Gunners, and his champions delivered a trademark performance.
At full-time at Villa Park, the travelling supporters sang about how they are going to win the league again with Arteta in charge.

articles.title: Sabalenka blocks out noise to start US Open 'three-peat' bid with victory
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka blocks out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".
body: The two-time defending champion has suffered a dip in form in recent months after a stellar start to the season in which she reached the Australian Open final and completed the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami.
Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under serious threat and she risks ending the year without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022.
However, she avoided an early slip-up as she held off a resilient Osorio to win 6-2 6-4 on her return to Arthur Ashe Stadium.
"I really feel my best emotions at this stadium so it means a lot to be back and have an opportunity for a 'three-peat'," Sabalenka said.

articles.title: Luke Murray adds UConn alums, former Dan Hurley star to Boston College coaching staff
articles.summary: New Boston College head coach Luke Murray has outlined plans to bring over many aspects of the UConn men's basketball program, from the Huskies' deliberate offensive approach to instilling a collective, team-first approach.
body: Murray placed the finishing touches on his debut coaching staff in Chestnut Hill over the past week, bringing yet more UConn flavor to his new home. The 41-year-old, first-time head coach hired three staff members with Connecticut ties last week, and on Monday afternoon, Murray hired Jared Terrell as a graduate assistant, one of Dan Hurley's best players during his time at Rhode Island.

Terrell, a consensus top-100 recruit out of Brewster Academy, marked a major early win for Hurley during his time in Rhode Island. The 6-foot-3 shooting guard shattered his lofty expectations with nearly 1,800 career points and a standout senior season, averaging 16.8 points on over 41% shooting from 3-point range for a Rhode Island squad that reeled off 16 straight wins and reached the NCAA Tournament Second Round. Terrell played one season on a two-way contract with Minnesota after he was not picked in the 2018 NBA Draft and made international stops in Turkey, Ukraine and Israel before his 2023 retirement.

articles.title: Pakistan drop seven players and release head coach
articles.summary: Pakistan respond to their series defeat by England by taking the extraordinary step of dropping seven players, calling up five uncapped players and releasing their head coach.
body: After two one-sided defeats in the first two Tests, the tourists have revamped their squad and backroom staff for the third and final match of the series at Edgbaston.

Five of the players dropped - Muhammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad - have featured in the series so far, while Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Jafar have been sent home without playing.
A total of seven players have been called up. Batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have previous Test experience and join the quintet of uncapped newcomers.
Spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, left-arm seamer Mohammed Imran Jr, wicketkeeper Said Baig and all-rounders Mohammad Imran and Razaullah have all received call-ups.

articles.title: Alcaraz makes winning return at US Open, Sabalenka safely through
articles.summary: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz didn't miss a beat as he returned from a four-month injury absence with a straight-sets first-round victory in the US Open on Monday.Poland's six-time Grand Slam singles champion Iga Swiatek sailed into the second round with a straight sets victory over China's…
body: Out of action with a wrist injury since April, Alcaraz passed his first test with flying colors, beating Russian Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 at Arthur Ashe Stadium, where women's defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also made it safely into the second round.

"It's been a really tough five months for me," Alcaraz said. "Being able to step on the Arthur Ashe, being able to compete again, I couldn't decide to come back in a better tournament. It's a really special place for me."
"I tried to enjoy as much as I can," he added. "I missed the crowd, I missed the energy, I missed competition. I missed everything."
Alcaraz is trying to bookend his season with Grand Slam titles after his Australian Open triumph in January made him the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam.

articles.title: 4 takeaways after Broncos set 17-player practice squad
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos announced their 17-player practice squad one day after forming the initial 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. As teams navigate through an 18-week schedule, there is a high likelihood that several of the players on this list will be needed for at least one regular-season…
body: Looking at the players on this list, there are some predictable names, but some of the bigger news is the players who aren't part of this team.
Here are some of the biggest takeaways following the practice squad being made official.

Fullback Adam Prentice and long-snapper Mitchell Fraboni were added to the practice squad, but the Broncos will elevate each of them for the first three games, in all likelihood. After that, they will have to either be released or added to the 53-man roster permanently.

Tight end Lucas Krull and offensive lineman Calvin Throckmorton fit the vested veteran status as well. In each case, these players did not have to clear waivers after being cut by the Broncos and the team does not have to guarantee their full salary for the season. Essentially, it's a smart way to maneuver around the system in order to create extra roster spots.

articles.title: Saka earns hard-fought win for Arsenal at Villa
articles.summary: Bukayo Saka's goal just before the hour mark was enough for champions Arsenal to maintain their perfect start with a 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park.
body: This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

articles.title: Fort Worth Star-Telegram issues damning TCU report after having credentials revoked
articles.summary: On August 26, the Fort-Worth Star Telegram reported that TCU banned the paper from covering all Horned Frogs athletics. According to the Star-Telegram, TCU rescinded its credentials over its reporting on a locker room fight.
body: TCU’s decision did not have the desired effect, as it did not intimidate the Star-Telegram out of reporting on the incident and its aftermath.

“TCU wide receiver Dozie Ezukanma was in the hospital for three days with injuries including a brain bleed and a concussion after teammate Jacob Fields punched and kicked him in the head, according to an arrest warrant affidavit,” Shambhavi Rimal of the Star-Telegram reported Monday.
Fields was dismissed from the team and has since been formally charged with aggravated assault causing serious bodily injury, as ESPN’s Mark Schlabach reported Sunday.

According to Rimal’s new Star-Telegram report, Ezukanma told the TCU Police Department that he had become unconscious after Fields allegedly punched him. Eventually, Curtis Talley Jr., the football team’s assistant athletic trainer, drove Ezukanma to the Harris Hospital emergency room.

articles.title: 'I'm so tired of the miserable haters' - Sabalenka hits back at critics
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka hit back at her critics, saying "haters can go and get on with their own lives" after she made a winning start in her quest for a ‌third successive US Open title.
body: Sabalenka is attempting to regain her usual dominance after a frustrating last six months, ​having failed to reach a final since she completed the Sunshine Double in March, but she made a confident start to her quest for a ‌rare 'three-peat' at the year's final major.
The world No 1 launched 32 winners to defeat Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4 in the first match of the day ‌on Arthur Ashe Stadium to set up a meeting with Russia's Polina Iatcenko in the second round.
Sabalenka, who was pictured at a pre-US Open event, has defended her stance saying "people love you or hate you".

"It took me a little while to shut down those noises," the four-time Grand Slam winner told Sky Sports Tennis. "There will always be people who support your choices, people who go against you, people who love you or hate you.

articles.title: McIlroy: 'Grumpy' world No 2 needs 'new goal' after FedEx Cup claims
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy needs to assess how much he truly wants to be world No 1 again alongside balancing his home life, according to former golfer Rob Lee.
body: The Northern Irishman finished in a seven-way tie for fourth at the FedEx Cup over the weekend, finishing five shots off tournament winner Scottie Scheffler despite showing earlier signs of promise.
Now 37, six-time major winner McIlroy admitted his "fuse was shorter than it used to be" before the final round at the East Lake Golf Club.
He had arrived in Atlanta off the back of three weeks of competing in a row, something he admitted he would never exceed again despite still managing a fourth-place finish over the weekend.
"That just tells you how good he is," Lee told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast. "But I think Rory's body language this week wasn't great. He looked slightly… is grumpy the right word?
